[table 0] Trait | Types | Definition | Function
Nesting | Ground | Nest is excavated in the ground; majority of species | Habitat requirement; impacts the richness and abundance of certain species as well as the overall diversity of the bee community
Stem | Nest is excavated in pithy stems, wood, pre-made cavities, and dead wood
Parasitic | Host nest is invaded by bee, who then lays own egg inside | Can be used to indicate and monitor host populations (Hudson et al., 2006; Sheffield et al., 2013)
Behavior | Solitary | Individual female establishes and provides for offspring alone | Differences in behavior can be linked to longer or shorter seasonal activity (Kratschmer et al., 2019)
Sub-social | Females may form loose colonies comprised of foundress and daughters
Eusocial | Establish colonies with divisions of labor
Parasitic | See above | See parasitic nesting
Lecty | Polylectic | Females are generalists and forage for pollen on a variety of plant taxa | Visits many different plants to collect nectar and pollen; have no morphological adaptations for pollen collection
Oligolectic | Females are pollen specialists and forage for pollen on closely related | Have specific morphological adaptations for pollen collection; tied to their host plant(s)

[table 4] Landscape | Solitary | Social | Cleptoparasitic
Organic | ~32 | ~1 | ~3
Conventional | ~20 | ~1 | 0
Meadow | ~29 | ~1 | ~4
